_metadata.description: Business Email Compromise scenario-specific derived parameters

base_rate_triangulation._citation: Three-anchor consensus: FBI IC3 (operational tempo), Verizon/IRIS back-calculation, Coalition insurer-adjusted
base_rate_triangulation.operational_tempo_note: FBI IC3 2024: 21,489 BEC complaints/$2.9B losses. Estimated 5-10x underreporting → 107k-215k actual events. Against ~6M US businesses → 1.8-3.6% LEF. Divide by susceptibility 10-30% → TEF 6-36%.
base_rate_triangulation.verizon_back_calculation_note: DBIR 2025: social engineering ~20% of breaches. BEC ~50% of social eng → ~10% of all breaches. IRIS all-incident LEF ~4.65%. BEC share → 0.47% LEF. Susceptibility 5-15% → TEF 3.1-9.4%. Widened range for uncertainty.
base_rate_triangulation.coalition_insurer_adjusted_note: Coalition overall claims 1.48% US. BEC estimated 15-25% of claims → 0.22-0.37% claims frequency. Bias correction 3.70x → 0.81-1.37% LEF. Susceptibility 10-30% → TEF 2.7-13.7%.

vector_proportions._citation: Derived from FBI IC3 2024, DBIR 2025, Proofpoint Human Factor 2025, Cofense 2026

bec_overall_share._citation: Derived from DBIR 2025 (social engineering ~20% of breaches, BEC ~50% of SE) + FBI IC3 (BEC is #1 by dollar loss)

bec_sector_shares._citation: Derived from FBI IC3 2024, DBIR 2025, NAIC 2025 BEC loss data. Not from IRIS (IRIS does not publish BEC-specific sector breakdown).

bec_revenue_shares._citation: Derived from FBI IC3 2024 + Coalition 2025. BEC targeting scales less steeply with revenue than ransomware — small businesses are also heavily targeted (payroll diversion, invoice fraud).

bec_revenue_prob_gte2._citation: Not available from IRIS for BEC specifically. All null — tool falls back to overall floor.

credential_tempo._citation: Derived from Flashpoint 2025 (1.8B compromised credentials), CrowdStrike 2025 (800% credential theft increase), FBI IC3
credential_tempo.note: BEC credential vector = account takeover via compromised business email. Tempo is lower than ransomware because BEC account compromise campaigns are more targeted.

exploitation_scanning._citation: BEC rarely involves exploitation. Minimal values reflecting edge cases (email server exploits, MFA bypass vulnerabilities).
exploitation_scanning.grn_malicious_rate_derivation: BEC exploitation is rare. Values reflect edge cases like Exchange ProxyLogon/ProxyShell used for email access, not typical scanning.
exploitation_scanning.grn_suspicious_rate_note: Not meaningful for BEC — exploitation is not a primary BEC vector.
exploitation_scanning.campaign_ip_ratio_note: Copied from ransomware. Rarely binding for BEC.
exploitation_scanning.poa_ransomware_note: For BEC, this is 'probability of email server exploitation leading to BEC' — very low.
exploitation_scanning.ransomware_proportion_note: Minimal. BEC operators almost never scan for exploitable infrastructure.

output_templates.one_sentence: Based on industry data, BEC operators {attempt_verb} organizations matching your profile roughly once every {recurrence_years:.0f} years (range: {low_yr:.0f}-{high_yr:.0f} years). This measures how often adversaries TRY -- not how often they succeed. Success probability depends on your controls (assessed separately).
